method.method_draft: First read the diagrams: Art’s trapezoid has parallel bases 3 in and 5 in with height 3 in; Roger’s rectangle is 4 in by 2 in; Paul’s parallelogram has base 3 in and height 2 in; Trisha’s right triangle has base 3 in and height 4 in. From the text, all cookies have the same thickness, all friends use the same total amount of dough, and Art makes 12 cookies. Compute each cookie’s face area: Art = ((3+5)/2)*3 = 12 sq in, Roger = 4*2 = 8 sq in, Paul = 3*2 = 6 sq in, Trisha = (1/2)*3*4 = 6 sq in. Since Art makes 12 cookies, the batch dough corresponds to 12*12 = 144 square-inch-thickness units. Divide 144 by each cookie area to get cookie counts: Art 12, Roger 18, Paul 24, Trisha 24. Therefore the fewest cookies are made by Art.
